query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled in situ oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) treatment in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy will precipitate uniformly dispersed nanoscale oxides (Al2O3/Cr2O3-like) that stabilize the lamellar architecture, impede dislocation motion, and suppress coarsening, leading to enhanced yield strength, improved creep resistance, and better corrosion performance while maintaining sufficient ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure derived from standard processing routes.
generation.intervention: Modified solution treatment at approximately 1100°C in a controlled, oxygen-rich inert atmosphere for 20–30 minutes to induce in situ oxide precipitation, followed by rapid quenching to freeze the dispersion.
generation.conditions: Control oxygen partial pressure during treatment to favor formation of stable Al2O3/Cr2O3-like oxide particles without over-oxidizing the material; ensure a rapid quench to maintain the fine distribution of the oxides.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed nanoscale oxide particles formed within the matrix and along lamellar boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The nano-oxides act as obstacles for dislocation motion and inhibit microstructural coarsening during thermal cycling, thereby enhancing strength and creep resistance while also providing a barrier to corrosion processes.
generation.predicted_outcome: The ODS-treated alloy is expected to exhibit significant improvements in yield strength and long-term creep resistance at both room and elevated temperatures, as well as enhanced corrosion performance under cyclic temperature fluctuations, compared to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: Standard AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy produced without ODS treatment.
generation.boundary: The benefits are expected under conditions where oxide particles remain stable (temperatures typically under ~800°C for extended periods) and when the oxygen partial pressure is precisely controlled. The performance gains may be limited if the oxide size and dispersion are not optimal or if the alloy is exposed to temperatures far exceeding the designed operating range.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the precise control of oxygen partial pressure to achieve the optimal oxide particle size and distribution, and how these parameters scale to industrial large-size production. The balance between improved strength/creep resistance and potential embrittlement also requires further validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set undergoing the modified solution treatment with controlled oxygen exposure (ODS-treated) and one set processed conventionally. Subject both sets to tensile tests at room and high temperatures, long-term creep tests under constant load, and corrosion resistance tests under cyclic temperature conditions.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength at various temperatures
Creep rate and time-to-failure under constant load
Corrosion performance via pitting potential and current density measurements
Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to characterize oxide particle size and dispersion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ODS-treated samples do not consistently show statistically significant improvements in mechanical properties (yield strength, creep resistance) and corrosion resistance relative to the standard alloy, or if microstructural analysis reveals an inconsistent or deleterious oxide distribution (e.g., coarsened or clustered oxides leading to embrittlement), then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

proposals.intervention: Minor Nb micro‐alloying combined with a post‐solution aging treatment
proposals.conditions: Introduce 1–2 at.% Nb during melting; perform a homogenization/solution treatment at ~1150°C for 1 h followed by a short aging step at ~750°C for 2 h
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of finely dispersed Nb‐rich precipitates preferentially situated along the lamellar interfaces
proposals.mechanism: These nano-precipitates act as dislocation pinning centers and reinforce the interlamellar regions, enhancing both strength and creep resistance while preserving ductility. The precipitates also contribute to microstructural stability under temperature fluctuations, mitigating coarsening during prolonged high-temperature use.
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility, enhanced room-temperature creep resistance, and better corrosion performance compared to the baseline alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention targets the main limitation—insufficient performance under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term loading—by stabilizing the lamellar structure via second-phase strengthening without compromising the overall toughness. The approach simultaneously meets industrial requirements for high-temperature stability, creep resistance, and corrosion tolerance.

proposals.intervention: Tailored thermal annealing to refine lamellar spacing
proposals.conditions: Subject the as-cast alloy to a two-step annealing process: an initial treatment at ~800°C for 1 h to activate diffusion, followed by a controlled cooling or a subsequent annealing at ~600°C for 4 h to refine the lamellar spacing
proposals.structural_mediator: Reduced and more uniform lamellar spacing along with possible interface segregation
proposals.mechanism: Refinement of the lamellar architecture increases the density of interfaces that impede dislocation motion, thereby raising strength. Optimized spacing also helps balance strength and ductility and enhances resistance to creep owing to more effective load partitioning at the refined interfaces.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A refined microstructure that exhibits higher yield strength and improved plasticity along with extended creep resistance under prolonged mechanical loading
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By tuning the microstructural scale without altering the alloy composition, this processing route directly improves the strength–ductility trade-off and mechanical stability under cyclic and extreme temperature conditions—a key industrial need for fasteners in aerospace applications.

proposals.intervention: Incorporation of in situ oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS)
proposals.conditions: Perform a modified solution treatment at ~1100°C in a controlled oxygen partial pressure (e.g., an oxygen-rich inert atmosphere) for a short duration (20–30 min) to induce the formation of nano-oxide particles, followed by rapid quenching
proposals.structural_mediator: Uniformly distributed nanoscale Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3-like oxide particles within the matrix and along lamellar boundaries
proposals.mechanism: These oxide dispersoids hinder dislocation motion and stabilize the microstructure during high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling. Their presence also acts as a barrier to grain coarsening, extending high-temperature performance and resisting creep deformation
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced high-temperature strength, improved resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion, while maintaining sufficient ductility, leading to a performance closer to or surpassing industrial requirements
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single intervention introduces a robust ODS mechanism to counteract issues related to high-temperature stability and environmental degradation, directly addressing the performance gaps of the starting alloy in aerospace fastener applications

proposals.intervention: Application of a high-temperature stable PVD nitride surface coating
proposals.conditions: Deposit a ~1–2 μm thick TiN (or AlN) coating using physical vapor deposition at moderate temperatures (~400°C) to avoid altering the bulk microstructure
proposals.structural_mediator: An adherent, nanocrystalline nitride surface layer tightly bonded to the substrate
proposals.mechanism: This hard, chemically inert coating serves as a protective barrier that reduces surface-initiated corrosion and wear, and minimizes the initiation of creep-related damage by limiting environmental effects and stress concentration at the surface
proposals.predicted_outcome: The coated alloy is expected to display significantly enhanced corrosion resistance and long-term mechanical stability under cyclic temperature fluctuations while retaining the inherent ductility and strength of the core alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The coating intervention directly enhances the material's environmental resistance and surface integrity under extreme conditions—which are critical for aerospace fastener applications—without necessitating alterations to the bulk lamellar structure or overall composition

decision.rationale: Incorporating an in situ oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) treatment directly targets the performance deficiencies by forming uniformly dispersed nanoscale oxide particles that can enhance high‐temperature strength, creep resistance, and corrosion tolerance while preserving ductility. This approach addresses the main industrial challenges for aerospace fasteners under cyclic temperature stress and long-term mechanical loading, and leverages a well‐established mechanism from ODS applications in other alloy systems.
